title: Polynomial sample bound in the dimension
statement: Let $n,C,Q$ be natural numbers, let $t>0$ be rational, and let $0<\varepsilon\le 1/2$ be rational. Assume $1\le n$, $1/(Q+1)\le\varepsilon$, and $t\le(C+1)(\sqrt{\lceil\log_2(n+1)\rceil}+1)$. Form the family size bound $B=(d+1)(c+1)^d$, where $d=\lceil 8t/\varepsilon\rceil$, $\theta=(\varepsilon/8)^2t^{-2}(1/9)^d$, and $c=\lceil2t/\theta\rceil$. Then the bounded-family sample count with family bound $B$ is at most $640\,2^{6e} (Q+1)^2 (n+1)^{3e}$, where $e=2a(b+1)$, $a=8(C+1)(Q+1)+1$, and $b=128(Q+1)^2(C+1)^3+4a+5$.
